facts.statement: Tethydraco was originally classified within the pterosaur family Pteranodontidae.
facts.quote: Tethydraco was originally assigned to the family Pteranodontidae.

facts.statement: Some researchers have debated whether Tethydraco was actually an azhdarchid or synonymous with the genus Phosphatodraco.
facts.quote: Some researchers argued that subsequently described material suggests that it may have been an azhdarchid, and possibly synonymous with Phosphatodraco, though this has been disputed.

facts.statement: The species Tethydraco regalis was formally described and named by Nicholas R. Longrich, David M. Martill, and Brian Andres in 2018.
facts.quote: In 2018, Nicholas R. Longrich, David M. Martill and Brian Andres described and named the type species Tethydraco regalis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in the late Maastrichtian deposits of the Sidi Daoui phosphate layers in Morocco.
facts.quote: The holotype, FSAC-OB 1, was found in the middle Couche III, itself the lowest phosphate layer complex at Sidi Daoui, dating from the late Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a single, relatively crushed left humerus bone.
facts.quote: It consists of a left humerus. The bone is relatively crushed.

facts.statement: Additional specimens referred to the species include ulnae, femurs, and a combined femur and tibia.
facts.quote: Other specimens have been referred to the species. FSAC-OB 199 is an ulna. FSAC-OB 200 is another ulna. FSAC-OB 201 is a thighbone. FSAC-OB 202 consists of a thighbone with shinbone.

facts.statement: The original authors noted that linking the holotype to other referred specimens is difficult due to a lack of overlapping bone material.
facts.quote: The describing authors admitted that a connection between the holotype and the referred specimens is hard to prove, in view of the lack of overlapping material.

facts.statement: Tethydraco lived approximately 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian stage in what is now Morocco.
facts.quote: Tethydraco is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period (Maastrichtian stage) of what is now the area of present Morocco, about 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Tethydraco had a wingspan of 5 meters and a body mass of 15 kilograms.
facts.quote: Tethydraco had a wingspan of 5 m and a body mass of 15 kg.

facts.statement: Tethydraco's humerus features a deltopectoral crest positioned proximally, near the torso and just proximal to the crista ulnaris.
facts.quote: In the humerus, the deltopectoral crest is placed rather proximally, closer to the torso of the animal, its closest border being positioned just proximal to the beginning of the opposite crest, the crista ulnaris.

facts.statement: The distal end of Tethydraco's humerus exhibits a broad triangular expansion.
facts.quote: Distally, away from the torso, the humerus has a broad triangular expansion.

facts.statement: Tethydraco's ulna is relatively short and wide, with a massively expanded proximal end.
facts.quote: The ulna is relatively short and wide while its proximal end, towards the humerus, is massively expanded.

facts.statement: In 2021, Labita and Martill reclassified Tethydraco as an azhdarchid, possibly synonymous with Phosphatodraco, based on wing morphology.
facts.quote: In 2021, Labita and Martill assigned a partial right wing (FSAC CP 251) from the same deposit to Tethydraco, but classified the genus as an azhdarchid possibly representing the wing-elements of Phosphatodraco based on its morphology, rather than a pteranodontid as originally proposed.

facts.statement: In 2023, Pentland and Poropat noted that the wing morphology of a specimen assigned to Tethydraco differs from the holotype, complicating its classification.
facts.quote: In 2023, Pentland and Poropat noted that while the hatchet-shaped deltopectoral crest of FSAC CP 251 is consistent with Azhdarchidae, it differs from the shape of the Tethydraco holotype.

facts.statement: Tethydraco coexisted with other pterosaurs like Phosphatodraco and the dinosaur Chenanisaurus in the Ouled Abdoun Basin.
facts.quote: It coexisted with the pterosaurs Alcione, Barbaridactylus, Simurghia and Phosphatodraco and the abelisaurid dinosaur Chenanisaurus.

facts.statement: The discovery of Tethydraco is considered evidence that pterosaur diversity in the Late Cretaceous was higher than previously thought.
facts.quote: Its existence was seen as proof that pterosaur diversity in the Maastrichtian was higher than previously assumed.

facts.statement: The existence of Tethydraco challenges the idea that pterosaurs went extinct earlier than the mass extinction event, suggesting the apparent decline was an artifact of the fossil record known as the Signor–Lipps effect.
facts.quote: Apparent pterosaur decline would have been an illusion caused by the Signor–Lipps effect, groups seeming to disappear earlier than a mass extinction because their youngest fossils by chance have been found at somewhat older layers than the extinction event.

facts.statement: Tethydraco had an estimated wingspan of about five meters.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado la envergadura de Tethydraco en unos cinco metros.

facts.statement: The deltopectoral crest on Tethydraco's humerus was positioned more proximally, closer to the body, than in other species.
facts.quote: En el húmero, la cresta deltopectoral se sitúa de una forma más proximal, es decir más cercana al torso del animal, con su borde más cercano posicionado proximalmente al inicio de la cresta opuesta, la crista ulnaris.

facts.statement: Tethydraco is classified within the family Pteranodontidae.
facts.quote: Tethydraco fue situado en la familia Pteranodontidae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis identified Tethydraco as the sister taxon to a clade containing Pteranodon and Geosternbergia.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico encontró que era el taxón hermano de un clado consistente de Pteranodon y Geosternbergia (= Pteranodon sternbergi).

facts.statement: Some researchers suggested that the humerus morphology indicated Tethydraco was an azdarchid rather than a pteranodontid, though later analyses confirmed it as a pteranodontid.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la morfología del húmero sugiere que Tethydraco sea en realidad un azdárquido, en lugar de un pteranodóntido como se propuso originalmente.

facts.statement: Tethydraco fossils were discovered in the Ouled Abdoun Basin in Morocco.
facts.quote: Tethydraco fue descubierto en la Cuenca Ouled Abdoun de Marruecos.

facts.statement: Tethydraco coexisted with other pterosaurs such as Alcione, Barbaridactylus, Simurghia, and Phosphatodraco, as well as the carnivorous dinosaur Chenanisaurus.
facts.quote: Allí coexistió con varios otros pterosaurios como los nictosáuridos Alcione, Barbaridactylus, Simurghia y el azdárquido Phosphatodraco, además del dinosaurio carnívoro Chenanisaurus.

facts.statement: Tethydraco lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The existence of Tethydraco demonstrates that pterosaur diversity in the Maastrichtian was greater than previously thought.
facts.quote: Su existencia es prueba de que la diversidad de los pterosaurios en el Maastrichtiense era mayor de los que se había considerado anteriormente.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the apparent decline of pterosaurs is an illusion caused by the Signor-Lipps effect, where the most recent fossils are found in older layers than the actual extinction event.
facts.quote: El declive de los pterosaurio sería una ilusión causada por el efecto Signor-Lipps, que se refiere a grupos que parecen desaparecer antes de una extinción en masa debido a que sus fósiles más recientes solo son hallados, debido a diferentes factores, en capas más antiguas que el propio evento de extinción.

rejected.quote: The generic name combines a reference to the Tethys, the ocean in the Late Cretaceous separating Africa from Europe and Asia, with a Latin draco, 'dragon'.
